derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and a compound of G303 (ἀνά) and G3396 (μίγνυμι);
def: to mix up together, i.e. (figurative) associate with

occurrences.text: I wrote unto you in an epistle not to company with fornicators:

But now I have written unto you not to keep company, if any man that is called a brother be a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or a railer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner; with such an one no not to eat.
And if any man obey not our word by this epistle, note that man, and have no company with him, that he may be ashamed.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
